note: Only the Megalithic Portal gives a point; no page with a quotable coordinate pair for the Tipitarillo yacata was found (news reports of the 2009 INAH communique give no coordinates).

Sources give period words only (Bronzo finale; fine Bronzo medio to età del Ferro) and Sardegna Turismo states the dating of the temple is uncertain between the Middle Bronze Age (16th-14th c. BC) and the Recent/Final Bronze Age (13th-9th c. BC), i.e. across buckets; one local site's 'databile al 1200 a.C.' contradicts the regional agency's uncertainty, so no reliable start.

Neither the English nor the Chinese Wikipedia article on the Fushan site prints a coordinate pair for it, and its Wikidata item Q110106780 carries no P625 statement. The Taipei Times page linked from the site is about Fongshan Old City in Kaohsiung, a different place, so no source can be quoted for this site's point.

No readable source dates the start of Koviljkin grad. English Wikipedia calls the ruins those of a Roman town and the German article says it was probably built as a Roman vicus, but neither gives a year, century or millennium for the site's foundation or first occupation; the Serbian article only says the Romans built it. Period words alone do not date a site.

No source gives a start year for Taqrachullu; the English article names the site and its National Cultural Heritage status without a date, and no readable excavation report with a first occupation date was found.

Wikipedia says only that Wraxall Camp (Failand, North Somerset) is an Iron Age settlement and that 1928 excavation found Iron Age-type pottery; that is a period word without a year, century or millennium, and no readable source gives a start date.

The only point found (Department of Archaeology and Museums record for the Naupura stupas, 35.8217, 74.2491) lies about 12 km south-south-west of Gilgit, while the same record puts the stupas 10 km west of Gilgit; no second source gives a point, so the stored point (Gilgit town centre) cannot be sourced or corrected.

No readable source gives a point for Allahdino: the Pleiades record 398671587 prints no coordinates in its visible text or in its JSON, the English Wikipedia article carries a Coord missing tag, and the Penn Museum expedition article prints no point.

Wikipedia only says the cup and ring marked stones of Ilkley Moor are dated somewhere between 3500 and 2500 years old, a class-wide range given in years ago for the moor's stones, not a year for the Nebstone's start.

Wikipedia and the MINCETUR inventory record call the site Inca without a year, century or millennium for its start; the dating study (Bauer et al., Andean Past) is a PDF the checker cannot read and no readable page states a start date.
Wikipedia calls it only a Chanka site; a culture name alone gives no year, and no source dates K'allapayuq Urqu.
Sources call La Amelia only a Pre-Columbian Maya archaeological site / small Late Classic site / polity; none names a more specific type with a type word.

The English Wikipedia article dates the site only relatively: 'Civilizations in the area date to around 4,000 years ago when prehistoric people settled there during the Neolithic age.' The Chinese article gives no absolute date either. A 'years ago' figure and the period word Neolithic are both excluded, so no source states a calendar year for the start.

Wikipedia in English, Spanish and French, Ayres's University of Oregon page on the Tahai research, the World Monuments Fund and the tourism pages name no year or century for the start of the Tahai complex; Ayres says only that the underlying Ahu Tahai unit is the earliest ahu dated so far, without giving the date.

No readable source prints a point for Troullos itself: its Wikipedia article and Wikidata item carry no coordinate, and the only nearby points found are for the municipal unit of Archanes, which is not the site's own place.
Wikipedia says the site was in use from Middle Minoan II until Late Minoan I, which is a period name without a year, century or millennium; no readable source gives a date for the start.

Wikipedia, Wikidata and Blom's 1928 article give no point; the only point found is a coarse GeoNames/Mapcarta entry (17 deg 25 min N, 89 deg 27 min W) that is not a clean quotable site point and cannot be tied to this site, so the stored point can be neither confirmed nor replaced.
source ancient_nerds, retired
The Pannonian Limes is a frontier line of several hundred kilometres along the Danube; Wikipedia and Wikidata give no point for it, and no source gives a single point for the site.

The English Wikipedia article on Lungkeng prints no coordinate pair for the site, and its Wikidata item Q122820786 carries no P625 statement. The settlement-geography page linked from the article concerns the settlement geography of Taiwan generally, so no source can be quoted for this site's own point.

The English Wikipedia article places Lungkeng in 'the pre-ceramic period, 5,000 to 6,000 years ago' and gives only a radiocarbon result, '5560±90 B.P., calibrated as 6385±170 B.P.'. A period word, 'years ago' and a BP date are all excluded, so no source states a calendar year for the start.

Wikipedia says only that the site was first settled in the Middle Preclassic period, a period word without a year; no readable source quotes a start year (the ceramic-sequence abstract giving 700 B.C. sits on a page the checker cannot read).

No source gives a point for Waman Pirqa that can be quoted. The English article has an empty coordinates field, the Wikidata item carries no P625, and the national inventory list for Ayacucho monuments has no entry for it (the only Lucanas entry, Racca - Raccay, has no coordinates either).

No source dates the start of Waman Pirqa. The English article gives only its name gloss, its location near Antamarka and its 2003 heritage declaration; no year, century or millennium for the site appears.
Wikipedia (en) lists K'ipakhara as missing geocoordinates and Wikidata has none; no readable source prints a point.
No readable source dates K'ipakhara.

The Devil's Highway is a Roman road from London to Silchester; no readable source (English, German or Italian Wikipedia, Wikidata, Commons) prints a point for it, and the stored point is in the City of London, not a sourced witness.

The stored point is Mundford village, about 2.5 km from the excavated site (NHER grid reference TL 8240 9484). The only readable sources for the site give a grid reference (not read) or the coordinates of a car park (Forestry England, Lynford Water); the Megalithic Portal, which prints degrees, refuses plain requests (403), so no quotable degree point for the site itself was found.

The Cultural Inventory record gives the monument's culture as Rome and no century, and the İzmir Bergama Museum text that names the Viran Kapı dates the colonnaded Via Tecta under Hadrian, not the gate itself; no source I could read dates the gate's construction, so I leave the field empty for the owner.
